sentences.text: Cheirolepis stands alone as the sole genus within its family and order.
This freshwater and estuarine predator reached a length of approximately 55 centimeters.
Its jaws could open wide enough to swallow prey measuring two-thirds of its own body size.
Well-developed fins provided the speed and stability needed for active hunting.
The species Cheirolepis trailli was first described by Agassiz in 1835 from Middle Devonian rocks in Scotland.
Large eyes suggest the animal relied on sight to locate food.
Taxonomically, the fish belongs to the parent group Actinopterygii.
It is further classified within the class Osteichthyes.
This organism inhabited waters from the Emsian to the Frasnian stages, between 410.62 and 372.15 million years ago.
